title: MSMAC: Accelerating Multi-Scalar Multiplication for Zero-Knowledge Proof
problem: Multi-scalar multiplication (MSM) is the most computation-intensive bottleneck in zero-knowledge proof generation. Existing CPU and GPU implementations are too slow for large-scale ZKP systems.
motivation: Accelerating MSM directly enables faster and more practical zero-knowledge proof systems for privacy-preserving cryptographic applications.
method: MSMAC proposes an FPGA accelerator with a custom instruction set architecture (ISA) optimized for MSM. It employs a pipelined Point Addition Unit (PAU) enhanced with hybrid Karatsuba multipliers for efficient elliptic curve arithmetic. A runtime system splits MSM tasks into optimal sub-tasks and orchestrates execution across Processing Elements.
key_novelty: Custom ISA design combined with pipelined Point Addition Unit optimization using hybrid Karatsuba multipliers specifically for MSM acceleration.
contributions: FPGA accelerator architecture specifically designed for large-scale multi-scalar multiplication
Custom instruction set architecture optimized for MSM operations
Pipelined Point Addition Unit with hybrid Karatsuba multiplier optimization
Runtime system for adaptive task splitting and Processing Element orchestration

metrics.speedup: 328X vs CPU single-core, 1.96X vs GPU, 1.79X vs ASIC, 1261X on 4 FPGAs vs single CPU

primary_theme: FPGA acceleration for cryptographic multi-scalar multiplication
